subject: Is the hessian available when fitting random effects in occu?

messages.author: 247b990d236a7af6
messages.subject: Is the hessian available when fitting random effects in occu?
parts:
I'm really glad to see there is the ability to include random effects in occu.

How does one obtain the hessian?  I've tried se = TRUE (which is what occu requires for models without random effects) and hessian = TRUE (which is what optim requires for obtaining the hessian) but the hessian does not show up in the output.

In fact one sees as part of the object returned:

..@ TMB             :List of 10
  .. ..$ par     : Named num [1:3] 0 0 0
  .. .. ..- attr(*, "names")= chr [1:3] "beta_state" "lsigma_state" "beta_det"
  .. ..$ fn      :function (x = last.par[-random], ...)  
  .. ..$ gr      :function (x = last.par[-random], ...)  
  .. ..$ he      :function (x = last.par[-random], ...)  
  .. ..$ hessian : logi FALSE
  .. ..$ method  : chr "BFGS"
  .. ..$ retape  :function (set.defaults = TRUE)  
  .. ..$ env     :<environment: 0x0000000009f1b920>
  .. ..$ report  :function (par = last.par)  
  .. ..$ simulate:function (par = last.par, complete = FALSE)  

Can the hessian be made available?

Thanks,

Jim

messages.author: 4f80e1927b0757cb
messages.subject: Re: Is the hessian available when fitting random effects in occu?
parts:
Hi Jim,

For a model 'fm' without random effects fit in TMB (with engine="TMB") you can get the hessian like this:

fm@TMB$he()

However TMB does not yet support this for models with random effects (you will get an error). Depending on what you are trying to do, it may be useful to get the joint precision matrix of fixed and random parameters using the TMB::sdreport() function:

jp <- TMB::sdreport(fm@TMB, getJointPrecision=TRUE)

see the docs for TMB::sdreport for more details on this and other stuff it can calculate from the TMB model object. I've been working on easier ways to get this info from unmarked e.g. via the vcov method.

Ken

Thanks again,

parts:
Sorry, my code was incomplete. 

The joint precision matrix is a component of the output object from sdreport, so something like this should get you what you want:

sdr <- TMB::sdreport(r2@TMB, getJointPrecision=TRUE)
jp <- sdr$jointPrecision

Ken
